title: India emerging as global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders and next-generation healthcare solutions: Jitendra Singh

ai.summary: India's Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that the country is becoming a global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders and healthcare solutions, with multiple research initiatives underway under the Ministry of Science & Technology and Department of Biotechnology.

facts.claim: India is emerging as a global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders and next-generation healthcare solutions
facts.quote: India is emerging as a global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders and next-generation healthcare solutions, with over a dozen diabetes-related research projects currently underway under the Ministry of Science & Technology, largely through the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and some through CSIR, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today.

facts.claim: Research is increasingly focused on the prevention and control of diabetes through next-generation molecular and genetic solutions
facts.quote: Emphasising that research is increasingly focused on the prevention and control of diabetes through next-generation molecular and genetic solutions, Dr. Singh said India’s vast population and genetic diversity offer a unique opportunity to develop scientific insights and healthcare solutions with relevance for the country and the world.

facts.claim: India has undergone a significant transformation in its scientific and healthcare capabilities
facts.quote: The Minister said India has undergone a significant transformation in its scientific and healthcare capabilities, moving from dependence on external solutions to developing indigenous vaccines, therapies, antibiotics and advanced medical technologies.

facts.claim: India has emerged as a frontline contributor to scientific research
facts.quote: He also referred to India’s vaccine pipeline for diseases such as HPV, dengue and malaria, and advances in genetic therapies, demonstrating the expanding scope of Indian biomedical research.

facts.claim: Research initiatives include an Indo-Danish collaborative study on gut microbiota among prediabetic and diabetic patients
facts.quote: Among the major research initiatives underway is an Indo-Danish collaborative study examining India-specific changes in gut microbiota among prediabetic and diabetic patients, aimed at advancing understanding of the role of gut microbial patterns in metabolic disorders.

facts.claim: Research involves genetically engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 capable of producing GLP-1
facts.quote: Another DBT-supported study involves genetically engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 capable of producing GLP-1, with the potential to be developed as a probiotic-based approach for delivering therapeutic molecules through the gastrointestinal tract, with human studies expected to be undertaken.
